title: Denied claims, reworked
short_title: Denied claims corrected, appealed or written off
brief:
A three-doctor family practice has **15 denied claims** across four payers.

**Recovered — $2,120:**
- 3 claims corrected with modifier 25
- One corrected to the rendering doctor's NPI
- A reconsideration proving timely filing
- A reconsideration citing the missed authorisation
- Write-offs only where nothing can win

**Left alone:**
- An intake rejection taken as proof of filing
- A duplicate whose original is in process
- A secondary claim before the primary paid
- Fixes that would land past the limit
- Claims already resubmitted and pending
promise: Every denied claim read by its reason code (a CO-16 corrected, a CO-197 checked for the authorisation, a CO-29 answered with proof of timely filing, a CO-18 left to wait for the original), fixed or appealed in the payer's own portal with the proof it needs, and written off only when it truly cannot be won — before the windows close.
persona: A three-doctor family practice billing four payers, with one part-time biller

fit.where_note: Each payer's own filing and appeal limits apply; the bench reads them in the portal.
fit.who: A small medical practice's biller working denied claims across several payers.
fit.not_for: A practice that cannot use a model path covered by a business associate agreement for real patient data.
fit.costs: No fees; only your Claude usage.

chore: Pull the denial worklist from the practice management system and read each claim's reason code. For a missing modifier or a wrong NPI, correct and resubmit — inside the payer's filing limit. For a timely-filing denial, find the clearinghouse report that proves the payer received the claim in time. For a missing authorisation, look it up in the payer portal. Never resubmit a duplicate, never file a secondary before the primary pays, never appeal what is out of time — and write off what cannot be won so it stops sitting on the books. Each payer's portal is different and UI-only.
command: Work this week's denial worklist: fix and resubmit what can be corrected, file a reconsideration where we have proof, write off only what can't be won, and leave anything still pending alone.

apps.name: Practice management
apps.role: the denial worklist, the claims, the encounter notes

apps.name: Clearinghouse
apps.role: acceptance reports: what each payer received, and when

apps.name: Availity
apps.role: payer rules, authorisations, corrected claims, reconsiderations
apps.api: No API for a small practice

steps: Reads every payer's filing and appeal limits in the payer portal before deciding anything.
Walks the worklist by reason code: CO-16, CO-18, CO-29, CO-197 and the rest.
Checks the encounter notes for the missing modifier and the rendering NPI.
Finds the clearinghouse acceptance report that proves a claim reached the payer in time.
Looks up the authorisation the claim left out.
Corrects, reconsiders or writes off each one — every act a card.

gates.label: Resubmit a corrected claim
gates.why: It reaches the payer; a bad resubmission becomes a duplicate or a timely-filing denial.

gates.label: File a reconsideration
gates.why: Most payers allow one; spending it without the proof loses the claim.

gates.label: Write off a balance
gates.why: It closes the claim in the books for good.

traps: A timely-filing denial whose only clearinghouse record is a rejection at intake: that is not proof the payer received it.
An authorisation denial with no authorisation on file: an appeal would be refused.
A duplicate-claim denial: the original is still in process. Never resubmit.
A correction that is right but would reach the payer on day 95 of a 90-day limit.
A secondary claim filed before the primary paid: wait for the primary EOB.
A reconsideration window of 180 days that closed 20 days ago.
Two denials already resubmitted and pending.
memory: Each payer's filing limit and reconsideration window, cited to the payer's own page.
Reason code to fix, per payer: what won last time.
Rendering NPIs per doctor, and which claims went out with the wrong one.
Which claims are already resubmitted, so none goes twice.

economics.basis: An estimate, and a gross one. A practice collecting about $70,000 a month with a 10 to 12% initial denial rate has about $7,000 to $8,400 a month denied ($70,000 x 11% = $7,700 at the middle). The roster's $4,200 a month is 55% of that middle figure, the share assumed recoverable and not already reworked by the biller. It is not netted against this practice's own rework rate, which no source gives: a practice whose biller already reworks most denials should count much less. The bench world alone holds $2,120 across fifteen denials.
economics.incumbent: Revenue-cycle outsourcers take about 4–9% of all collections, not just the denials; in-house, reworking one claim costs a practice around $25 of staff time.

sources.label: Experian State of Claims: ~11.8% initial denial rate (2024)
Aptarro: the cost of reworking a denied claim
Prospyr: filing limits across major payers
MedCity / KFF: prior-authorisation denials and overturn rates (2025)

caveat: Real patient data needs a model path covered by a business associate agreement. This playbook's bench runs on synthetic claims only.

edge.difficulty_why: Three systems, payer-specific rules and windows, reason codes that each want a different remedy, and proof that lives in a batch report.
edge.usefulness_why: Thousands of dollars a month that a small practice leaves on the table for want of a biller's hours.

expectation.why: A good biller recovers most of it in an afternoon; the bar is most of the money, no duplicate resubmission, nothing filed out of time.

lessons.title: A dropped op is told in the same turn too
lessons.found: Her first ops of a session were dropped, the turn ended with nothing in flight, and every later tab starved for claim ids: 2 of 10, $0.

lessons.title: Tool results are bounded by the frame's budget, not a count
lessons.found: She read twelve pages in one turn and saw eight; four re-reads every turn.
